stem.text: The function p is continuous and \( p(t) > 0 \) for all t. Let \( G(x) = \int_{0}^{x} -\left(t - 3\right)\left(t - 10\right)p(t)\,dt \) for \( 0 < x < 6 \). Find the value of x in \( 0 < x < 6 \) at which G has a critical point, and determine whether G has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither there. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: At x = 3 only; G has a relative minimum there because G' changes from negative to positive at x = 3.

worked_solution.text: \( G'(x) \) is \( -\left(x - 3\right)\left(x - 10\right) \) times \( p(x) \), which is positive, so \( G'(x) = 0 \) only where \( -\left(x - 3\right)\left(x - 10\right) = 0 \), at x = 3 and x = 10.
Only x = 3 lies in \( 0 < x < 6 \); x = 10 is greater than every x in the range.
On the range the factor \( \left(x - 10\right) \) keeps one sign, so G' changes from negative to positive at x = 3, and G has a relative minimum there.

options.label: At x = 3 only; G has a relative minimum there because G' changes from negative to positive at x = 3.
At x = 3 only; G has neither there because G' stays close to 0 on both sides of x = 3.
options.derivation: the point classified by the size of the derivative nearby rather than by whether its sign changes

options.label: At x = 3 and x = 10; G has a relative minimum at x = 3 and a relative maximum at x = 10 because G' changes sign at each.
options.derivation: the zero x = 10 of the derivative kept although it lies outside the stated range

options.label: At x = 3 only; G has a relative maximum there because G' changes from negative to positive at x = 3.
options.derivation: the direction of the sign change read the wrong way round in the classification
